STANMERE PEDAL FREIGHT CO-OPERATIVE
Operations & Finance Committee, meeting of Thursday 17 September 2026
Paper 4: Query from Kōwhai Lane Dispensary, invoice SPF-2608-114
Prepared by Sanne Sato (dispatch coordinator) for Kwame Okafor (treasurer)

1. Background
Kōwhai Lane Dispensary has used us for prescription runs since March 2025 on the standard account rate: $9.50 per drop inside the ring road and $14.00 outside it. Their August invoice, SPF-2608-114, came to $3,412.60 incl. GST. On 4 September their practice manager, Halle Whitlock, emailed to dispute the waiting-time charges and to ask for a 12% credit "for the late runs".

2. Facts
- We charge waiting time at $0.60 per minute after the first 10 minutes at pick-up.
- The invoice shows 386 minutes of waiting time in August, which comes to $231.60.
- The dispensary says most of the waiting happened because riders were told to turn up before scripts were ready. They say they never asked for early pick-ups.
- Late runs: our log shows 9 of 212 drops delivered outside the agreed window. The dispensary counts 14. The logs for 19 to 21 August were lost when the dispatch tablet was reset on the 22nd, so we cannot check those days.
- The 12% is asked on delivery charges only. August delivery charges were $2,640.00 ex GST.

3. Options
A. Keep the invoice as issued. No credit. The account is worth about $3,000 a month*, and Halle has said they are "looking at alternatives".
B. Waive waiting time for August. Credit 341 minutes, $204.60 + GST (as amended: Kwame's recount found two pick-ups on 12 August entered twice). Late-run credit refused.
C. Give the 12% on delivery charges, $316.80 + GST, and keep the waiting time.

4. Recommendation
Option B. From 1 October, dispatch should stop sending riders to Kōwhai Lane before the confirmed ready time. This should make further waiting-time charges unlikely. The late-run claim can't be settled either way until the dispensary sends the drop references for the five runs we have no record of.

* The $3,000 figure is the 2025 monthly average. Since February 2026 the dispensary has sent its after-hours work elsewhere, and its monthly billing has been between $2,350 and $2,700. August was higher than usual because of the clinic's flu-vaccine mail-out.

q1.instructions: The waiting-time credit proposed under Option B covers every minute of waiting time shown on the August invoice.

criteria.true: The minutes credited under Option B equal the minutes of waiting time the invoice bills for.
criteria.false: Option B credits fewer minutes than the invoice bills for.

q2.instructions: Before GST, the credit the dispensary would receive under Option C is larger than the credit it would receive under Option B.

criteria.true: The ex-GST amount credited under Option C exceeds the ex-GST amount credited under Option B.
criteria.false: The Option C credit is equal to or smaller than the Option B credit, ex GST.

q3.instructions: How many of the August drops were actually delivered outside the agreed window?

criteria.nine_late_drops: The co-op's own log figure is the correct count.
criteria.fourteen_late_drops: The dispensary's count is the correct figure.
criteria.cannot_tell_from_document: The paper does not allow the true count to be fixed either way.

q4.instructions: Place the risk that the co-op loses the Kōwhai Lane account if the committee chooses Option A (keep the invoice as issued, no credit).
criteria: Low: nothing in the paper suggests the dispensary is likely to leave over this dispute.
Moderate: the dispensary has signalled some dissatisfaction, but there is no sign it has yet shifted work away.
High: the dispensary has both voiced an intention to look elsewhere and already moved part of its business away.

NORTHGATE SOUND ROOMS, HARROWGATE
Studio Management Meeting, 18/04/2023
Paper 4: Complaint, invoice INV-2291 (L. Jansen)
For decision by: the Producer
Prepared by: Fenna Zielinski, Bookings

1. Background
Leonie Jansen records her interview series with us on Thursdays. On 06/04/2023 she wrote to dispute the overrun charge on INV-2291, which covers her session of 23/03/2023. She says the session ran late because the desk failed, and that she should not pay for time lost to our equipment.

2. Facts
The session was booked 10:00–13:00 in Studio 2, with Jonas Nakamura engineering. The overrun billed was 95 minutes, charged at £48 per half hour or part of one: 4 units, £192.00 plus VAT.

According to Jonas, the desk dropped out at about 11:20 and the session was paused while he rebooted and re-patched it. He estimates this took around 30 minutes. Once that time is taken out, the chargeable overrun is 65 minutes, as amended, and the 95 on the invoice should be disregarded.

Rate card terms (section 6.2): overrun on standard-rate bookings is charged at £48 per half hour from the booked end time. Block-booked clients receive 15 minutes' grace, after which overrun is charged at £36 per half hour.

Ms Jansen bought a block in January 2023. The 23/03 session was the thirteenth she has used from it. Our system records the block as 12 sessions. Her email says she paid for 15. We have not yet found the January receipt, and the payment line on the account reads "Block – JANSEN – £1,575".

3. Options
A. Keep INV-2291 as issued: £192.00. Ms Jansen has said that if we do, she will move her remaining recordings elsewhere. At current frequency that is roughly £420 a month.
B. Reissue at the standard rate on 65 minutes: 3 units, £144.00.
C. Reissue at the block rate on 65 minutes less 15 minutes' grace (50 minutes): 2 units, £72.00. Credit the difference against her next session.

4. Recommendation
Option C, if the block is confirmed as 15 sessions. If it was 12, Option B. Either way, Bookings will apologise in writing about the desk fault.

Jonas has also asked for the Studio 2 desk power supply to be replaced (quote £310), but that is outside this paper.

F.Z.

*The 65-minute figure comes from Jonas's handwritten session sheet. The desk's own log was lost in the reboot. Jonas says the stop time of 14:05 is "near enough, could have been a few minutes either side". The first unit boundary after grace falls at 13:45 and the second at 14:15, but under option B a stop before 14:00 would bring the charge down to 2 units.

BEXLEY CROSS ICE CENTRE
Operations Management Meeting – 28/03/2023
Agenda item 4
Paper ref. BX/23/041
Author: Rhea Oduya, Duty Operations Supervisor

Resurfacer hydraulic failure, Saturday 11/03/2023

1. Background

1.1 At approximately 14:40 on Saturday 11/03/2023, during the interval resurface between public sessions, a hydraulic hose on the ice resurfacer split near the conditioner housing. Oil was deposited across the north end of the pad before the machine was stopped. The incident was logged as BX/23/041.

1.2 The 15:00–16:30 public session was cancelled. 212 tickets had been sold for it, at £7.50 adult and £5.50 junior.

1.3 The Bexley Cross Raiders junior squad were booked on the pad from 17:00 to 19:00. Under the club hire agreement, if the Centre cancels with less than two hours' notice a goodwill payment of £150 is due in addition to the hire refund. The front desk log shows the club secretary was phoned at 15:10. The Raiders' coach recalls the call coming "just before three".

2. Facts

2.1 Lars Mbeki (Ice Technician) estimated the spill at 6 litres on the day. His written report of 13/03 gives "8–10 litres, hard to tell with the melt".

2.2 An area of roughly 18 m² was scraped back and rebuilt overnight. The pad reopened at 10:00 on Sunday 12/03, one hour late.

2.3 One member of staff slipped while laying absorbent. No injury was reported and no accident book entry was made until 14/03.

2.4 Public refunds: cash refunds were offered to anyone who asked before 23:59 on 25/03/2023. After that, credit vouchers only. 141 tickets have been refunded in cash, totalling £958.50. 23 vouchers have been issued since 26/03. The other 48 ticket holders have not been in touch.

3. Options

A. Replace the failed hose only. Parts £380, engineer call-out £240. Total £620.

B. Replace the full hydraulic hose set (8 hoses) and pressure-test. Total £2,150.*

C. Option B, plus a fitted drip tray and a written pre-use hose check added to the resurfacer daily sheet. £2,150 plus £460. Total £2,610.

The temporary repair fitted on 11/03 is holding but is not rated by the manufacturer.

4. Recommendation

That Option B be approved, with the daily sheet amendment from Option C done in-house at no extra cost. A decision is requested from the Rink Manager, Tamsin Lowry, on whether to pay the Raiders the £150.

* The £2,150 figure is from the supplier quotation ref. BX/23/041, dated 16/03/2023, valid to 31/03/2023, excluding VAT. On inspection Lars counts nine hoses on our machine, not eight. The supplier has not yet said whether the ninth is included.

HARROWGATE STREET MARKET — MANAGEMENT COMMITTEE
Paper MC/23/41 — Meeting of 24 August 2023
Item 6: Result of safety check, Lane B
Prepared by: Sanne Xavier, Assistant Inspector
For decision by: Efe Thorne, Market Inspector

1. Background

1.1 A routine safety check of Lane B was carried out on Wednesday 9 August 2023 between 10:15 and 12:40. Fourteen stalls were checked. Twelve were found compliant. Stall 29 had a loose awning pole, which was fixed on the day.

1.2 Stall 31 is held by Farid Quigley. It was first licensed in October 2021 as Class P (packaged and dry goods). Mr Quigley pays a licence fee of ₹1,200 per month and is up to date.

1.3 Market Rule 14(b) applies to Class H (heated food) stalls only. It limits each stall to two LPG cylinders of 14.2 kg on site, and requires a clearance of at least 1.5 m between any burner and the stall's rear sheeting.

2. Findings at Stall 31

2.1 Three cylinders were on site: two connected and one spare under the counter.

2.2 Clearance from the rear sheeting was measured at 0.9 m.*

2.3 A fire extinguisher was present, last serviced in January 2023.

2.4 Mr Quigley said the third cylinder had been delivered that morning and the empty one would be collected "by Friday". No collection was recorded at the follow-up visit on 16 August.

2.5 After the change of trade approved at the committee meeting of 12 May 2023, Stall 31 has traded under a Class H licence, selling fried snacks and tea.

2.6 A notice was issued to Stall 31 in March 2023 for a counter overhang onto the walkway.

3. Options

Option A: Written warning and re-inspection within 14 days. No cost to the market.

Option B: Penalty of ₹2,500 under Rule 14(b). Removal of the third cylinder and repositioning of the burner within 7 days. Re-inspection staff time is estimated at ₹600.

Option C: Move the stall to end bay 52, which has a deeper pitch. Shelter and drainage works are estimated at ₹18,000. Bay 52 carries a fee of ₹1,450 per month.

4. Recommendation

Option B is recommended. The burner can be moved forward within the existing pitch, and the stallholder has agreed to remove the spare cylinder.

Prepared by: Viggo Mbeki, Seed Bank Curator

1. Background
Freezer 3 in the vault holds long-term storage collections at a set point of −20 °C. During the night of 18 to 19 March the compressor tripped after a load-shedding changeover. The standby generator ran, but the freezer circuit did not reset.

2. Facts
2.1 The data logger recorded the first reading above −15 °C at 01:40 on 19 March. Rhea Costa (Facilities) reset the breaker on arrival. Her work order gives the time the freezer was without cooling as 435 minutes.
2.2 The highest temperature logged was −4.5 °C. The logger reads every 30 minutes, so the actual peak may have been higher.
2.3 Freezer 3 holds 212 accessions. All are in sealed foil packets at about 5% moisture content.
2.4 174 of these were banked before 1 March 2023 and have an initial germination result on file. The other 38 came in from the Cederberg collecting trip after that date. They went into the freezer straight from drying and have not had a baseline test.
2.5 The temperature was back below −18 °C at about 09:10.

3. Options
A. Retest all 212 accessions at R145 per accession: R30 740.
B. Run baseline tests on the 38 post-cut-off accessions and retest a 10% sample (18) of the older accessions: 56 tests, R8 120.
C. Make no retests. Add an excursion flag to all 212 records in the collections database. Staff time is estimated at 6 hours. There is no external cost.

4. Recommendation
Option B. The older accessions were dry, sealed and above freezing for just over six hours, so their seeds are unlikely to have lost much viability. The 38 newer accessions have no reference result, and this cannot be put right later. Under any option, Pia Guerrero (Records Officer) will need to decide whether the excursion flag goes on all 212 records or only on those that are tested.

Viggo Mbeki
24 March 2023

1. Background
Coastline Optical Lab has made almost all of our prescription lenses since 2019. On 11 April they moved their surfacing work to a new site at Bellbrook. Total: $4,297

Since 22 May the lab has been back to about 8 working days. Their rep, Dale Okoro, told me the Bellbrook site is "settled now". He also offered a credit of 8% against our April and May invoices, which comes to about $1,150.¹

Efe Haldane (Optometrist) reports two complaints passed on through patients' health funds. Neither has gone any further.

Option A: Stay with Coastline and accept the credit.
No added cost. The risk is that delays come back with no fallback in place.

Option B: Move all prescription work to Harbourline Lens Co.
Harbourline charges about $6.50 more per pair. At our usual volume of around 140 pairs a month, that is about $910 a month extra. It also means new frame tracing settings and two days of retraining for the dispensing staff.

At about 45 progressive pairs a month, the extra cost is around $292.50 a month. Single vision work, which was less affected, stays where it is.

Committee meeting, 21/06/2023
Agenda item 6: Hose stock discrepancy, members' store
Paper by Marcus Jansen, Treasurer

1. Background
The store sells garden hose to members by the metre, cut from a bulk reel. A new 200 m reel was bought from the usual supplier on 14/03/2023 for £210.00 (£1.05/m). We sell it at £1.40/m. Ivo Strand, who runs the Saturday store, keeps the cut-and-sale sheet on the clipboard by the till.

2. The figures
Sales recorded on the sheet from 18/03/2023 to 10/06/2023 come to 80 m across 11 sales, with £112.00 taken. That should leave 120 m on the reel.
Ivo measured the reel on 10/06/2023 and got 269 ft on his tape. The sheet in the store now shows the remaining stock as 82 m, which leaves 38 m unaccounted for. At selling price that is £53.20; at cost it is £39.90.
There is nothing unusual in the cash. The tin balanced on every Saturday checked.

3. A previous case
In autumn 2021 the manure bay came up 14 bags short (25 kg bags, £4.50 each, £63.00 in total). That was written off and a padlock fitted to the bay. Those bags were left outside the store in an open bay, so the circumstances were different. The hose reel is kept inside the locked store.

4. Options
A. Write off the shortfall at cost (£39.90) and take no further action.
B. Write off as in A, and also buy a padlock and chain for the reel bracket (£18.50) so that only store volunteers can cut lengths.
C. Write off as in A, and add a monthly measured count of the reel to the store rota. This costs nothing except about 15 minutes of volunteer time a month, a quarter of an hour that Ivo has already said he can find.

5. Recommendation
Option B, with the monthly count from Option C added. I don't think the shortfall is large enough to justify more than this, but the 2021 experience suggests that a physical lock settles these matters faster than a reminder in the newsletter.

M. Jansen

From: Nadia Carlisle, Stores Officer

1. Background
Pre-orders for the winter seed potato order closed on 31 January. Forty-one members ordered 406 kg across five varieties. We ordered 18 x 25 kg sacks from Ardmoyle Seed Supplies at €31.50 per sack, plus €45.00 delivery. The invoice total was €612.00 and it has been paid.

2. Facts
The pallet arrived on Wednesday 4 March. Tamsin Mbeki signed the driver's docket for 18 sacks. On the Saturday after, Aoife Fitzgerald and I weighed out the stock for collection and found the following:

Variety | Pre-ordered kg | Sacks ordered | Sacks on shelf | kg weighed
British Queen | 118 | 5 | 5 | 125
Charlotte | 96 | 4 | 3 | 70
Kerr's Pink | 52 | 3 | 3 | 75
Rooster | 98 | 4 | 4 | 100
Sarpo Mira | 42 | 2 | 2 | 49
Total | 406 | 18 | 17 | 419

One Charlotte sack was missing. One of the three that were there is labelled 25 kg but weighed 20. That leaves Charlotte members 26 kg short, or 27% of what they ordered. Kerr's Pink has 23 kg left over after pre-orders. At invoice price the missing sack is worth €31.50, about 5% of the invoice.

We reported the shortage to Ardmoyle on Monday 9 March. Their terms only cover shortages reported within 48 hours of delivery. They have offered a €15.00 goodwill credit against next season's order.

3. Options
A. Buy one 25 kg sack of Charlotte at Coyle's Garden Centre for €38.00 and pay for it from general funds. Charlotte members get their full order. The 23 kg of Kerr's Pink goes to the stall at €1.50/kg.
B. Reduce each Charlotte allocation pro rata to about 73% of the amount ordered and refund the difference at €1.26/kg. That comes to €32.76 across 9 members. Kerr's Pink goes to the stall as in A.
C. Offer the 23 kg of Kerr's Pink to Charlotte members in place of the missing stock, at no charge. Refund at €1.26/kg anyone who declines. If everyone declines, the cost is the same as B. If everyone accepts, there are 3 kg of refunds (€3.78).

4. Recommendation
Option A. It costs the most in cash, but no member gets less than they paid for. Charlotte is also the variety most members on the lower field asked for by name.

Note: Aoife thinks the store's hanging scale reads light, possibly by 1–2 kg per sack. That could put the Charlotte figure of 70 kg nearer 75. Tamsin has since said she signed for 18 sacks from the docket and the pallet wrap and did not count them one by one. Operations Meeting, 12 March 2026
Paper OM/26/07

Trade Account eligibility: Sunrise Residency PG, Station Road

Prepared by: Jyoti Winterbourne, Supervisor, Station Road branch
For decision: Quentin Lowry, Area Manager

1. Background

Under the Trade Account terms (rev. August 2024), account holders get 12% off self-service wash cycles. To qualify, an applicant must hold either GST registration or a Shop & Establishment licence, and must have used at least 40 hours of machine time per calendar month, averaged over the previous three months.

Sunrise Residency, a 22-bed paying-guest house run by Mr R. Bhandari, applied on 26 February. The PG is not registered for GST. It has a receipt dated 9 January 2026 for a Shop & Establishment licence application, but the licence has not been issued. In his covering letter, Mr Bhandari says the PG uses the machines "more than 43 hours every month" and puts his saving at about ₹2,630 a quarter.

2. Facts

Machine time from loyalty card records:
December 2025: 2,610 minutes*
January 2026: 2,280 minutes
February 2026: 2,470 minutes (to 26 Feb)
Three-month average: 2,453 minutes

Spend over the same period: ₹21,940 in total. Of this, ₹13,200 was wash cycles, ₹6,480 was dryers and ₹2,260 was detergent and other sales.

The PG uses the branch mostly between 7 and 10 a.m. on weekdays, which is not our busy period.

3. Options

A. Refuse the application until the licence is issued. This costs nothing directly, but it risks losing a customer worth ₹21,940 a quarter. A rival self-service outlet opened on Canal Street in January.

B. Approve a provisional account until 30 June 2026, with a copy of the licence to be produced before that date. At current usage, the discount would cost about ₹1,584 a quarter.

C. Decline the Trade Account and offer a Gold loyalty upgrade, which gives 5% off all services. This would cost about ₹1,097 a quarter at current spend.

4. Recommendation

Option B. The machine-time requirement is met. The licence application was made before the request, and the PG's usage falls outside peak hours.

* Oisin Jokinen (Accounts) points out that the December figure includes use on 18 and 19 December under card ending 4471. That card is registered to a resident, Ms P. Kaur, not to the PG. Mr Bhandari says this use was for the PG's bed linen while the PG's own card was being replaced. The records do not separate that use from Ms Kaur's personal washes, so the PG's actual December total cannot be confirmed from the card data.

1. Background

The committee approved replacement of the Tītoki Saddle VHF repeater at the June meeting. Purchase order 23-041 was raised with Ridgeline Comms Ltd on 14 June for $8,640 incl. On 30 August Marcus Yilmaz (Ridgeline) told us the unit was held up overseas. His current date is 6 October, but he would only say "likely".

2. Current position

Since 22 August the north catchment has had no repeater coverage. We have hired two satellite handsets at $45 per day each.* Hire to 20 September comes to $2,610.

During the callout on 9 September (incident 23-041, injured tramper above Kōwhai Hut) the field party had no comms with base for about 40 minutes. The patient was extracted without further harm. The debrief noted the gap but did not find it changed the outcome.

3. Options

A. Wait for Ridgeline. Keep the hire going to 6 October, about a further $1,440. Marcus has offered a 5% credit on the invoice ($432). Risk: the date moves again.

B. Cancel and reorder from Southpeak Radio. Quote $9,950 incl. GST, delivery 10 working days from order, install extra at about $600. Ridgeline's terms allow cancellation but keep the $1,200 deposit.

C. Wait for Ridgeline, but end the hire and borrow the two spare handsets Police SAR have offered. No hire cost. They can recall them at 24 hours' notice.

For comparison, when the Unimog was delivered seven weeks late in 2019, the dealer paid $1,800 under a late-delivery clause and covered the hire vehicle. The Ridgeline order has no such clause. Alberto Bello (Treasurer) reads clause 9 of their terms as allowing a claim for "reasonable costs". Ridgeline does not agree.

4. Recommendation

Option A, with a firm date to be got in writing from Ridgeline by 29 September. If they do not give one, move to Option B. Alberto supports this. I would note that the operations subcommittee was split between A and C.

Agenda item 6: Claim by trader, Pitch 22 (Claim ref. MK-0931)
Paper prepared by Priya Gallo, Markets Officer, for Carys Fitzgerald, Market Inspector

1. Background
Sanne Varga has held Pitch 22 (dried flowers, cards and paper goods) on a standing licence since March 2021. Overnight on 8–9 October the standpipe at the Mill Lane end of the market failed at the joint. Ms Varga's stock was stored in the lock-up beside the standpipe as normal. When she opened at 06:45 on Wednesday 9 October the floor was under water.

2. Facts
The water meter showed 3,400 litres used between the 18:00 reading on 8 October and the 07:30 reading on 9 October. The night patrol note records the leak as "seen running 02:10, reported." The contractor attended under job MK-0931 at 08:20 and thought the joint had probably been weeping since early evening. Ms Varga's email of 10 October says "the best part of 750 gallons went through my stock."

Items claimed, from her email and the receipts she attached:
- Dried flower bunches, 46 at €8.50 — €391.00
- Greeting cards and wrapping paper, per supplier invoice 3317 — €212.40
- Display cloths, 4 — €64.00
- Two storage crates of mixed stock, contents not listed — approx. €150

There is a receipt for the cloths but no invoice for the crates. Ms Varga also missed the Saturday 12 October market and says she lost a day's takings, but she has not put a figure on it.

3. Options
A. Pay the claim in full as submitted from the market maintenance budget (€4,100 remaining this year).
B. Pay only the evidenced lines (flowers, cards and paper, cloths). Ask for an itemised list for the crates and decide on it separately.
C. Pass the claim to the Council's public liability insurer. The policy excess is €500 per claim, which the market budget pays. Last year the insurer took 11 weeks to settle a similar claim.

4. Recommendation
Option B. The standpipe is market infrastructure, and the patrol note shows we were told about the leak at least four and a half hours before the trader arrived. The Inspector to confirm whether a lost-trading element can be considered at all under the licence terms.

PENDLE WATER BREWING CO.
Management Meeting, Thursday 21 November 2024
Paper 4: Complaint from Saffron Yard Kitchen regarding Invoice PW-2411
Prepared by: Nadia Varga, Sales & Accounts
For decision by: Ravi Brandt, Head Brewer

1. Background
Saffron Yard Kitchen has taken our draught pale ale since March 2024. On 15 November their owner, Mr Joglekar, emailed disputing two items on Invoice PW-2411 dated 4 November and has withheld payment of the full invoice, ₹82,200, until it is resolved.

2. The facts
Invoice PW-2411 carries:
- 6 × 30 L kegs Pale Ale at ₹9,800 = ₹58,800
- Keg deposit, 6 × ₹3,500 = ₹21,000
- Line cleaning service (4 lines) = ₹2,400

The first point is the keg count. The customer says five kegs arrived. The delivery note signed on 4 November shows five. A sixth keg went out on 7 November on the Thursday van run, and their bar staff signed for it. The invoice count of six is therefore correct, although it was raised three days early.

The second point is the line cleaning. Farid Fairweather attended on 12 November. His job sheet records arrival at 15:40 and departure at 16:05. He cleaned lines 1 and 2. Lines 3 and 4 were connected to kegs that were in service during the lunch-to-dinner changeover, and the bar manager asked him not to disconnect them. The job sheet does not record that he arranged to come back.

The customer also says the beer was hazy. Those kegs were filled from brew batch PW-2411. The retained sample from that batch tested at 1.8 EBC on 6 November, which is within our limit of 2.0. Farid's note says lines 3 and 4 had not been cleaned for around five weeks, and that is the more likely cause.

3. Options
A. Credit the full cleaning charge, ₹2,400. No revisit. Settles quickly. Lines 3 and 4 stay uncleaned.
B. Credit half, ₹1,200, and return to clean lines 3 and 4 at an agreed time before 30 November. Revisit cost about ₹650.*
C. Make no credit and offer to clean lines 3 and 4 at no extra charge. Revisit cost the same as B, but the customer is likely to stay unhappy about the keg count.

4. Recommendation
Option B. Send the customer a copy of the 7 November delivery note with the credit note so that the keg question is closed at the same time.

* The ₹650 covers van fuel and cleaning chemical only. Farid estimates 1.5 hours on site plus travel. On that basis, the revisit costs more than the ₹1,200 credited under Option A.

ASHCOMBE RIDING STABLES
Management Meeting – Tuesday 14 November 2023
Paper MM/23/41: Indoor school allocation, Saturday mornings in December
Prepared by: Farid Tremblay, Head of Instruction
For decision by: Yard Manager

1. Background
1.1 Since 2 September the indoor school has been booked every Saturday from 0830 to 1130 for the Junior group lessons. There are three back-to-back lessons of six riders, charged at $55 per rider.
1.2 On 6 November Quentin Kaur (Livery Coordinator) confirmed a series of dressage clinics for livery clients with visiting coach Imani Petrov. They are on Saturdays 2, 9 and 16 December, 0900 to 1300, in the indoor school. The outdoor arena cannot be used because it is being resurfaced until the second week of January.

2. The facts
2.1 The bookings overlap from 0900 to 1130 on all three dates, which is 2.5 hours each Saturday.
2.2 Junior lessons bring in 18 × $55 = $990 per Saturday, or $2,970 over the three dates.
2.3 The yard charges an arena fee of $25 per clinic rider. With 8 riders* this comes to $200 per Saturday, or $600 in total. Ms Petrov's fees are paid to her direct by the clients.
2.4 In April 2022 the Pony Club rally clashed with lessons. The lessons were moved to the outdoor arena, which cost $180 in extra staff time over two weekends and lost no income. That route is not open this time.

3. Options
Option A – Move the Junior lessons to Sunday mornings on the three dates. Parents have been asked informally, and about a third say they cannot attend on Sundays. Expected loss is around $330 per Saturday ($990 in total), plus about $150 in extra Sunday staff cover.

Option B – Move the clinic to 1130–1530. Floodlights would be needed from about 1500 at $40 per hour. Juniors are not affected. The cost to the yard is about $40 to $60 per date. Ms Petrov has not yet said whether she can work the later times.

Option C – Hire the covered arena at Ridgeway Equestrian, 6 km away, for the clinic at $150 per half-day. Clients would have to transport their own horses. Several have no lorry.

4. Recommendation
Option B, if Ms Petrov confirms she can work the later slot by 20 November. If she cannot, Option A.

* The figure of 8 comes from the October sign-up sheet. Since then the livery office has received 11 names, but Q. Kaur says two or three of these may be sharing a slot or riding half-sessions only. The final number had not been confirmed at the time of writing, and arena fee income could be anywhere from $200 to $275 per date.

OAKHAVEN MOUNTAIN LIFTS — SUMMER OPERATIONS COMMITTEE
Meeting of 12 June 2025
Paper SOC/25/14
Prepared by: Priya Strand, Lift Operations Manager
For decision by: Vera Varga, Patrol Leader (evacuation sign-off)

1. Background
Marcus Xavier, event secretary of Oakhaven Harriers AC, has asked us to run the Line 2 chair (Ridge Quad) outside normal summer hours on Saturday 21 June 2025 for the club's Midsummer Ridge Run. Normal summer close is 17:30. The request is for uplift from 19:00 to 21:30, carrying an estimated 180 runners and spectators to the top station, with downloading from 21:00.

In June 2023 we ran an evening uplift for the same club on Line 1 (Quarry Double). That approval was based on a maximum ground clearance of 9 m, a full rope evacuation time of 50 minutes and two patrollers on standby. Line 1 is closed this summer for bullwheel replacement, so those figures do not carry over.

2. Facts
Line 2 length: 1,140 m; 62 chairs; 4 seats each.
Maximum ground clearance: 46 ft, span T7–T8 (manufacturer drawing, 1998).
Estimated full rope evacuation time: 95 minutes¹.
Sunset on 21 June: 21:57. Patrol standard requires evacuation complete by sunset plus 30 minutes.
Patrollers required on standby: 4, plus one lift operator and one top-station attendant.
Club has offered a hire fee of €1,150.

3. Options
A. Refuse. No cost. Club would run the course on foot only and has said it would move the start to 18:00.

B. Approve as requested, 19:00–21:30. Staff overtime estimated €1,420 (6 staff × 4 h at average €59.20/h incl. PRSI). Net cost to us after hire fee: €270.

C. Approve a shortened window, 19:00–20:30, uplift only, downloading by foot path. Staff overtime estimated €900 (5 staff × 3 h, rounded). Net income: €250. Last chair leaves the base at 20:30, giving 1 h 27 min of daylight beyond the evacuation estimate.

4. Recommendation
Option C. It meets the club's main need, keeps us within the sunset rule with margin, and covers its own cost. Recommend approval subject to the Patrol Leader's sign-off on evacuation cover.

P. Strand

¹ The 95-minute figure is from the April drill, which used the two 30 m rope kits. Both 30 m kits went to the supplier in Ballyfin for inspection on 28 May and are not due back until 4 July. The kits currently in the summer store are the 12 m units.

Paper PM-07/25
Date of meeting: Thursday 23 January 2025
Prepared by: Imani Yeo, Unit Location Coordinator
For decision by: Vera Carlisle, Location Manager

Late delivery of Main Street shopfront facades

1. Background

The art department ordered six painted shopfront facades for the Main Street block (Sc. 38–44) from a contracted scenic workshop. Delivery was due to the lay-down yard behind the Tollerton Memorial Hall by 7:00 am on Tuesday 14 January. The facades came in at 4:40 pm on Thursday 16 January, after the trucks were held up at the workshop and then again by the weight check on the Highway 9 bridge. Soren Zielinski (Construction Manager) confirmed that all six panels arrived undamaged. Each is 4.2 m wide and 3.6 m high.

Because the shoot was planned around the facades, Main Street could not be shot on 14 or 15 January.

2. Costs already incurred

Crew stand-down, 14 January (half day, call cancelled late): $8,400
Council road occupancy permit, extension to 22 January*: $1,150
Overnight security on the closed block, 2 nights: $960
Compensation to traders, 6 shops at $350: $2,100
Total to date: $13,060

The workshop's agreement includes a late-delivery clause (cl. 11.3). The daily rate in our signed copy was left blank. Soren believes "about $500 a day" was agreed by phone in November, but the workshop has not confirmed that figure.

3. Options

Option A: Shoot Main Street on 21–22 January, inside the permit extension. This bumps the Kearney Rd interiors to 24 January. Estimated extra cost: $4,700 (overtime for the art department to dress the panels over the weekend, plus a second traffic management crew).

Option B: Move Sc. 38–44 to Wattle Lane, which already has an approved permit. Wattle Lane has room for four facades, not six, so Sc. 41 would need to be rewritten. Estimated extra cost: $6,250, which includes re-dressing and $1,800 to move the panels.

Option C: Shoot only Sc. 38–40 on Main Street on 22 January and pick up the rest as inserts in the week of 3 February. Estimated extra cost: $3,200 now, plus a second permit application of unknown cost.

4. Recommendation

Option A is recommended. It keeps all six facades and the original block, and the traders already know the dates. We would still pursue the workshop under cl. 11.3 for 14–16 January.

* The council officer quoted $1,150 over the phone on 15 January. The confirmation letter has not yet arrived. The officer said the fee "may be calculated per day of extension" and not as a single flat fee. If so, the true figure would be higher. One of the six traders (No. 17, the bakery) has not yet signed the compensation form.

Paper SM-25/38: Invoice query, Harbourline Media (INV-25-0417)
Prepared by: Jonas Whitlock, Studio Manager

1. Background

Harbourline Media records its weekly series "The Long Table" in Studio B. On 15 October we sent invoice INV-25-0417 for two items. Marcus Abernathy, Harbourline's production lead, wrote on 21 October to dispute both.

2. The facts

2.1 Session of 7 October. The booking was for 4 hours at $85.00 per hour. The engineer's session sheet records 270 minutes from first mic check to last file transfer. Our rate card bills overruns in 30-minute blocks. The invoice charged 5.0 hours, which is $425.00. On the rate card the charge should be 4.5 hours, which is $382.50.

2.2 Session of 14 October. A 3-hour session was booked to start at 10:00. Under clause 6 of our terms, a booking cancelled at least 48 hours before its start gets a full refund less a $15.00 admin fee. A cancellation inside that window is charged at 50%. The cut-off was therefore 10:00 on Sunday 12 October. Mr Abernathy's cancellation email arrived at 10:40 on 12 October. The invoice charged 50% of $255.00, which is $127.50.

2.3 The invoice totalled $552.50 before GST, and $602.23 including GST at 9%.

3. Options

A. Leave the invoice as issued. No change.

B. Correct the 7 October line to 4.5 hours and keep the late-cancellation charge. This reduces the invoice by $42.50 before GST, to $510.00 ($555.90 with GST).

C. Correct the 7 October line, and replace the late-cancellation charge with the $15.00 admin fee. This reduces the invoice by $155.00 before GST, to $397.50 ($433.28 with GST).

4. Recommendation

Option B. The overrun was billed incorrectly and should be put right. The cancellation email arrived 40 minutes after the cut-off, and clause 6 has been applied the same way to other clients this year.

FILE NOTE

By: Wes Jokinen, Arranger

Operations Committee – Paper 14/26
Meeting of Tuesday 8 December 2026
Prepared by: Dev Gallo, Bookings Coordinator

Extended ice hire request, 31 December 2026 – Stanmere Curling Club

1. Background
On 27 November Lars Delacroix, secretary of the Stanmere Curling Club, wrote asking to hire the main sheet from 9.30 pm on 31 December to 1.30 am on 1 January for a members' bonspiel and New Year function. The Arena normally closes at 10.00 pm on New Year's Eve. The club has hired off-peak ice on Thursday evenings since March 2026 without incident.

2. Facts
Hire requested: 4 hours at the community rate of $185 per hour, $740 excl. GST.
Expected numbers: 46 on the ice. Mr Delacroix's letter gives "about 60" for the function afterwards.
Refrigeration, lighting and resurfacing: estimated $210.
Staffing: the After-Hours Use Policy (clause 6.2) requires two staff on site for any booking running past 11.00 pm, one holding a current first-aid certificate. An affiliated club with its own approved safety officer may run with one staff member.
Staff cost: two staff for 4.5 hours including close-down, $612; one staff member, $306.

In 2024 the Stanmere Junior Ice Hockey Association hired the rink until midnight on New Year's Eve, 3 hours at the then rate of $160 per hour, with one staff member. That booking showed a net loss of $95.

The club is affiliated to the regional curling association. "Affiliated club" in clause 6.2 means a club entered on the Arena's own Affiliated User Register. The club's application to the register was received on 30 November and is due before this committee in February.

Bram Jansen, who is rostered as duty supervisor on 31 December, has checked the roster costs. Because the holiday rate moves to double time from midnight, the staff figures, as amended, are $684 for two staff and $342 for one.

3. Options
A. Decline the request. No cost, no income.
B. Approve with two staff. $740 less $684 less $210: a shortfall of $154.
C. Approve with one staff member, treating the pending application as sufficient. $740 less $342 less $210: a surplus of $188.
D. Approve until 11.00 pm only, at 1.5 hours ($277.50), with one staff member under standard rates.

4. Recommendation
That the committee approve Option B, with the club asked to meet the shortfall by way of a $150 after-hours surcharge, and that the duty supervisor be given discretion on the night to end the session early if numbers exceed those stated.

Dev Gallo
2 December 2026

Management Meeting – 14/12/2023
Paper 4: Claim from pitch 31 (J. Strand) – awning damage

Prepared by: Sanne Yeo, Site Manager

1. Background

Mr Jonas Strand arrived on Wednesday 06/12/2023 for a four-night stay on hardstanding pitch 31, booked at £28.50 per night. On the evening of Thursday 07/12/2023 a limb came off the ash at the northern boundary during high winds and fell on his porch awning, tearing the roof panel and bending two poles. Mr Strand left a night early, on the Friday morning, and emailed his claim the following Monday. He is asking for the cost of a replacement awning (about £600) and a refund of the nights he did not use.

2. Facts

At 14:30 on the Thursday reception put up a high-wind notice and sent a text to all guests on the register, asking for awnings to be taken down by 18:00. Clause 11.4 of our booking terms says awnings left standing after the time given in such a notice are at the owner's risk.

Wes Abernathy, Head Warden, logged the branch down at 17:25. Mr Strand's photograph of the damage is timestamped 17:31. The ash was last looked at in the tree survey of 21/11/2023 and was not flagged.

Mr Strand has sent a retailer quote of £612.40 for a replacement awning of the same type. Unused pitch fees come to 2 nights, £57.00. A third night, the Friday, had already been taken, as he did not leave until after 11:00.

3. Options

A. Pay the claim in full: £612.40 plus £57.00 refund, total £669.40.
B. Goodwill payment of half the awning quote, £306.20, plus the £57.00 refund, total £363.20.
C. Decline the awning claim under clause 11.4 and refund the unused nights only, £57.00.

4. Recommendation

That the meeting approves Option A and that the bookings office arranges payment to the card used for the booking. The tree belongs to the park and the notice gave a clear time; I do not think clause 11.4 can be relied on here. Our insurance excess is £500, so a claim under the policy would not save us much.

* The £612.40 is the current price for a new awning. Mr Strand has sent his original receipt from May 2019, which shows £455.00. If the meeting would rather pay what he actually spent, Option A comes to £512.00 and Option B to £284.50.

2. Policy
Section 4.2 of the Equipment Policy (revised April 2023) says personal kit damaged on a callout will be reimbursed at current replacement cost, less 20% for each full year of age, for full operational members. Trainees are covered for team-issued kit only.

Management meeting, Tuesday 25 November 2025
Paper 3: Late screen consignment from Kestrel Parts (Order KP-55817)

Prepared by: Elin Kettle, Workshop Lead
For decision by: Ivo Oduya, Shop Manager

1. Background
Order KP-55817 was placed on 3 November for 40 replacement display assemblies (mixed models), with delivery promised for 6 November. Kestrel has been our main screen supplier since March 2024 and has been late twice before, by one day each time.

2. Facts
2.1 The consignment did not arrive on the promised date. The goods-received sheet shows it booked in on 14 November. Kestrel's rep messaged Fenna on WhatsApp on 13 November saying the boxes had been "dropped at your back door on the 12th". There is no courier slip on file.
2.2 Jobs waiting on these screens: 23, with an average wait of 7 working days against our quoted 2.
2.3 Goodwill already given at the counter: R2,940, mostly as labour discounts at Fenna's discretion.
2.4 Kestrel has offered a 12% credit by way of apology.
2.5 Four customers collected their phones unrepaired. Two have left one-star reviews.

3. Options

Option A: Accept the Kestrel credit and take no further action.
Cost to us: nil beyond the R2,940 already given.

Option B: Accept the credit and issue a R150 voucher to every affected customer who has not yet had a discount. On 26 jobs (as amended, since Fenna found three more in the walk-in book), less the 11 already discounted, that is 15 vouchers, R2,250.

Option C: Move screen orders to Duinekop Components, who quote next-day delivery to Marlow Ridge. Their unit prices run about R45 higher on our usual models. At roughly 55 screens a month, that is about R2,475 a month extra.

4. Recommendation
Option B for the current backlog. Keep Kestrel for now, but place a trial order of 10 screens with Duinekop in December so we have a working second supplier before the January rush.

Elin Kettle
20 November 2025

Note on 2.4: The 12% applies only to the value of the delayed consignment, R18,600 excl. VAT, which gives R2,232. It does not apply to our November account with Kestrel, which stands at R41,200. Kestrel's rep, Fenna and I have each confirmed this in writing.

6. Handling contribution
6.1 Partner agencies pay a handling contribution of 6% of the book value of all stock collected in a calendar month. It is invoiced on the 5th of the following month.
6.2 Book value is as shown on the collection docket, not retail value.

7. Storage checks
7.1 Each agency holding chilled or frozen stock is checked once in every 12-month period. That check carries no charge.
7.2 If a check records a fail on any temperature item, a follow-up check must be completed within 21 days. Follow-up check fee: $85.00 per visit.
7.3 Chilled storage must read at or below 5°C, and frozen at or below -18°C. A reading no more than 0.5°C above the limit is recorded as marginal, not as a fail.
7.4 Chilled and frozen allocations are suspended from the date of a fail until a follow-up check is passed.

8.1 Category C agencies (volunteer-run with no paid staff, annual turnover under $50,000) pay 40% of the fee in 7.2. The reduction does not extend to clause 6.
8.2 If a fail is caused by a power interruption confirmed in writing by the utility provider, the fee in 7.2 is waived for agencies in all categories.

9.1 Queries on clauses 7 and 8 are decided by the referrals officer.

Total: $629

Option C. The wrench fault and the missing initials are separate gaps and each option closes only one of them. The claim is to be paid under the branch excess. The insurer has not yet confirmed the excess for this policy year. Last year it was $1,500.

L. Fairweather

UPTON VALE DONOR CENTRE
Operations Meeting, 26 June 2025
Paper 4: Donor claim, I. Oduya (ref. DC-2025-0617)
Prepared by: Bronwyn Brandt, Donor Care Coordinator

1. Background

On 11 June 2025 Mr Ivo Oduya donated whole blood at the Upton Vale fixed site. Needle out was recorded at 10:42. At about 10:51, while at the refreshment table, he had a vasovagal reaction and fell. Staff nurse Xiu Rasmussen attended him. He had no injury needing referral and left at 11:35. His spectacles were broken and his phone screen was cracked in the fall.

On 16 June Mr Oduya submitted a written claim for compensation.

2. Amounts claimed

Replacement spectacles: R3,850*
Phone screen repair (quote): R2,190
Loss of earnings, 12 June (one day): R1,400
Total: R7,440

3. Applicable policy

Under the Donor Care Policy (section 7.3), the site may make an ex gratia payment of up to R2,500 without referral to the insurer, for a reaction or fall during the 15-minute post-donation observation period. This applies only to regular donors, defined as donors with at least three whole-blood donations, including the current one, in the preceding 24 months. All other claims go through the public liability policy, which has an excess of R5,000 per incident.

Donor record: Mr Oduya first donated at this site in 2023 and donated again on 4 February 2025. The 11 June donation was his third.

4. Options

Option A: Ex gratia payment of R2,500 under section 7.3. This would be paid from the site's donor care budget, which has R6,200 left for the 2025/26 year. Mr Oduya would be told that this is the maximum the site can pay without referral.

Option B: Refer to the insurer. Because the claim is below the R5,000 excess, the site would carry all of it anyway, plus about three weeks of administration. Claims for loss of earnings are normally declined.

Option C: Pay R6,040 in full for the spectacles and phone, leaving out loss of earnings. Anything above R2,500 needs the regional manager's approval.

5. Recommendation

Option A. The fall happened inside the observation period, and the nurse's notes show that Mr Oduya was seated with a juice for about four minutes before he stood up without telling staff.

* The spectacles figure was given by Mr Oduya by telephone on 18 June. The written optometrist quotation, received on 23 June, is R3,150 for frames and lenses. The difference is a R700 eye test, which he says he needed in order to get the replacement made. If the eye test is excluded, the claim total is R6,740.
